13:2.sourceText: τῆς φιλοξενίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε· διὰ ταύτης γὰρ ἔλαθόν τινες ξενίσαντες ἀγγέλους.
13:2.targetText: Do not be forgetful of hospitality, for through this some entertained messengers unaware.

groups.note: The actual ἔλαθον is the finite escaping-notice/unawareness predicate used with an entertaining participle. English turns that real unawareness head into unaware while making the entertaining action its main finite verb; it is not a different original ignorance noun.

The actual ξενίσαντες is an aorist hospitality/entertaining participle under the unawareness predicate. English presents it as the main finite entertained in the same unaware-hospitality construction.

13:3.sourceText: μιμνῄσκεσθε τῶν δεσμίων ὡς συνδεδεμένοι, τῶν κακουχουμένων ὡς καὶ αὐτοὶ ὄντες ἐν σώματι.
13:3.targetText: Be mindful of those in bonds, as having been bound with them, of those maltreated, as yourselves also being in the body.

groups.note: The actual prisoners noun δεσμίων is described in English as in bonds, and these same actual people are the partners of the immediately following bound-with comparison. English them resumes those real prisoners without a second written pronoun or a substituted Greek bonds noun.
The actual συνδέω compound supplies the together-with binding predicate; its with force belongs to that compound, while the actual prisoners named above supply the partnership referent.
The actual αὐτοί is the intensive yourselves with the addressed people in context. It is not a separately printed reflexive ἑαυτοί form.

13:4.sourceText: Τίμιος ὁ γάμος ἐν πᾶσιν καὶ ἡ κοίτη ἀμίαντος, πόρνους γὰρ καὶ μοιχοὺς κρινεῖ ὁ Θεός.
13:4.targetText: The marriage [is to be] honored by all, and the bed undefiled, for God will judge whoremongers and adulterers.

groups.note: The actual τίμιος is an adjective, honorable/valued, rendered honored. The English is-to-be frame remains supplied; no passive τιμάω honoring verb is printed.

The actual ἐν πᾶσιν can denote among all people or in all respects. LSV by all construes the honorable-marriage description through the community’s honoring; this does not print a passive-agent ὑπό or settle the persons/respects interpretation from the form alone.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a prescriptive copular frame to the honorable-marriage nominal clause; no corresponding finite Greek be or passive honor verb is written.

13:5.sourceText: Ἀφιλάργυρος ὁ τρόπος, ἀρκούμενοι τοῖς παροῦσιν· αὐτὸς γὰρ εἴρηκεν Οὐ μή σε ἀνῶ οὐδ’ οὐ μή σε ἐγκαταλίπω·
13:5.targetText: [Be] without covetous behavior, being content with the things present, for He has said, “No, I will not leave, no, nor forsake you,”

groups.note: The actual ἀφιλάργυρος is the privative not-money-loving adjective modifying conduct. English without covetous expresses that same negative property as a preposition/adjective phrase, not a separately printed Greek without word or a claim about every kind of desire.

The two actual σε objects name the same addressed person under the coordinated leaving and forsaking predicates. English states you once at the end for both; both real source object identities remain in that genuinely shared final object.
The actual first-person aorist subjunctive leaving verb belongs to the emphatic negative promise; English I will leave is not a written Greek future indicative.
The actual οὐ μή reinforces the negative under the preceding nor connector. English no renders the pair together, without inventing an additional English not.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an imperative be frame for the Greek nominal conduct-without-money-love prescription. No corresponding Greek be imperative is printed.

13:6.sourceText: ὥστε θαρροῦντας ἡμᾶς λέγειν Κύριος ἐμοὶ βοηθός, οὐ φοβηθήσομαι· τί ποιήσει μοι ἄνθρωπος;
13:6.targetText: so that we boldly say, “The LORD [is] to me a helper, and I will not fear what man will do to me.”

groups.note: The actual confident/being-bold participle θαρροῦντας is rendered adverbially as boldly qualifying our saying; it is not an independently written Greek adverb.

The actual τί introduces the rhetorical question what will man do to me. LSV incorporates it as the content of not fearing; the same what/action/person relation remains, while its direct-question versus dependent-content construction is explicit.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.
English adds a coordinating and before the not-fearing declaration; pinned N1904 has no conjunction at that point.

13:7.sourceText: Μνημονεύετε τῶν ἡγουμένων ὑμῶν, οἵτινες ἐλάλησαν ὑμῖν τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὧν ἀναθεωροῦντες τὴν ἔκβασιν τῆς ἀναστροφῆς μιμεῖσθε τὴν πίστιν.
13:7.targetText: Be mindful of those leading you, who spoke to you the word of God, who, considering the outcome of [their] behavior, imitate [their] faith:

groups.note: The actual genitive relative ὧν identifies the leaders whose faith is to be imitated, with their conduct’s outcome considered in the same instruction. LSV splits that possessive-relative relation as who plus two bracketed their possessors. The real same leaders own both conduct and faith; this does not turn the source genitive into a nominative subject or invent two additional written Greek possessives.

13:8.sourceText: Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐχθὲς καὶ σήμερον ὁ αὐτός καὶ εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας.
13:8.targetText: Jesus Christ—the same yesterday and today and for all ages.

groups.note: The actual definite plural the ages is rendered all ages, expressing the unlimited collective span rather than a separately printed πᾶς all quantifier.

13:9.sourceText: διδαχαῖς ποικίλαις καὶ ξέναις μὴ παραφέρεσθε· καλὸν γὰρ χάριτι βεβαιοῦσθαι τὴν καρδίαν, οὐ βρώμασιν, ἐν οἷς οὐκ ὠφελήθησαν οἱ περιπατοῦντες.
13:9.targetText: Do not be carried away with strange and manifold teachings, for [it is] good that by grace the heart is confirmed, not with meats, in which they who were occupied were not profited;

groups.note: The actual passive confirming infinitive has the heart as its accusative subject; English expresses that same content as that the heart is confirmed. The finite/complement frame does not invent a second Greek that or be verb.
The actual βρώματα means foods, rendered by the older broad English meats. The source is not the more specific flesh-meat noun κρέα.

The actual present walking/conduct participle περιπατοῦντες names those following the food regimen. LSV were occupied recasts that conduct as a past-state phrase; the source remains the actual walking/conduct head, not an invented occupied passive verb.

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

13:10.sourceText: Ἔχομεν θυσιαστήριον ἐξ οὗ φαγεῖν οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἐξουσίαν οἱ τῇ σκηνῇ λατρεύοντες.

13:11.sourceText: ὧν γὰρ εἰσφέρεται ζῴων τὸ αἷμα περὶ ἁμαρτίας εἰς τὰ ἅγια διὰ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως, τούτων τὰ σώματα κατακαίεται ἔξω τῆς παρεμβολῆς.
13:11.targetText: for of those beasts whose blood is brought for sin into the holy places through the chief priest—of these the bodies are burned outside the camp.

groups.note: The actual genitive animals noun belongs to the relative whose-animals/blood construction; English fronts it as of those beasts and separately says whose blood. Those is nominal support for that actual relative-animal set, not an independently written Greek demonstrative.
The actual burning verb is singular with a neuter plural bodies subject in Greek; English uses plural are burned for those same bodies.

13:12.sourceText: διὸ καὶ Ἰησοῦς, ἵνα ἁγιάσῃ διὰ τοῦ ἰδίου αἵματος τὸν λαόν, ἔξω τῆς πύλης ἔπαθεν.
13:12.targetText: For this reason, also Jesus—that He might sanctify the people through [His] own blood—suffered outside the gate;

groups.note: The actual own adjective ἴδιος identifies the blood as belonging to the acting Jesus. English His makes that same own-blood possessive relationship explicit; no additional αὐτοῦ pronoun is written.

13:14.sourceText: οὐ γὰρ ἔχομεν ὧδε μένουσαν πόλιν, ἀλλὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν ἐπιζητοῦμεν.
13:14.targetText: for we have no abiding city here, but we seek the coming one.

groups.note: The actual feminine coming/to-be participle is substantive of the desired city, inherited from the preceding city noun. English one supplies that real future-city designation; it does not change this feminine city modifier into a masculine personal Coming-One title.

13:15.sourceText: δι’ αὐτοῦ οὖν ἀναφέρωμεν θυσίαν αἰνέσεως διὰ παντὸς τῷ Θεῷ, τοῦτ’ ἔστιν καρπὸν χειλέων ὁμολογούντων τῷ ὀνόματι αὐτοῦ.
13:15.targetText: Through Him, then, we may always offer up a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips, giving thanks to His Name.

groups.note: The actual ὁμολογέω participle denotes confessing/acknowledging/praising His Name, rendered giving thanks in this praise context (Thayer3670 cites the use). It remains that real confession/acknowledgment head, not a fabricated εὐχαριστέω thanksgiving verb or an independent giving predicate.

13:16.sourceText: τῆς δὲ εὐποιΐας καὶ κοινωνίας μὴ ἐπιλανθάνεσθε· τοιαύταις γὰρ θυσίαις εὐαρεστεῖται ὁ Θεός.
13:16.targetText: And do not be forgetful of doing good and of fellowship, for God is well-pleased with such sacrifices.

groups.note: The actual εὐποιΐα is the good-doing/beneficence noun; English doing good verbalizes that one noun, without separate original do and good words.

13:17.sourceText: Πείθεσθε τοῖς ἡγουμένοις ὑμῶν καὶ ὑπείκετε· αὐτοὶ γὰρ ἀγρυπνοῦσιν ὑπὲρ τῶν ψυχῶν ὑμῶν ὡς λόγον ἀποδώσοντες· ἵνα μετὰ χαρᾶς τοῦτο ποιῶσιν καὶ μὴ στενάζοντες· ἀλυσιτελὲς γὰρ ὑμῖν τοῦτο.
13:17.targetText: Be obedient to those leading you, and be subject, for these watch for your souls, as about to give account, that they may do this with joy, and not sighing, for this [is] unprofitable to you.

groups.note: The actual middle/passive πείθεσθε is the persuasion/obedience form used here of heeding leaders. English be obedient preserves that contextual use without replacing it by a different Greek obey verb or treating every πείθω occurrence as an unconditional obedience instruction.
The actual ὑπείκω means yield/give way; English be subject retains that yielding predicate, not a different printed ὑποτάσσω verb.

The actual future giving-back participle ἀποδώσοντες describes those who will render account. English about to give expresses that prospect; the source has no separate μέλλω about-to verb, and the future form alone does not set a calendar imminence.

13:18.sourceText: Προσεύχεσθε περὶ ἡμῶν· πειθόμεθα γὰρ ὅτι καλὴν συνείδησιν ἔχομεν, ἐν πᾶσιν καλῶς θέλοντες ἀναστρέφεσθαι.
13:18.targetText: Pray for us, for we trust that we have a good conscience, willing to behave well in all things,

groups.note: The actual πείθομαι is we are persuaded/confident; English we trust denotes that conviction about conscience. The actual persuasion/confidence head remains distinct from a different πιστεύω believing verb.

13:21.targetText: make you perfect in every good work to do His will, doing in you that which is well-pleasing before Him, through Jesus Christ, to whom [is] the glory through the ages of the ages! Amen.

13:22.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, ἀνέχεσθε τοῦ λόγου τῆς παρακλήσεως· καὶ γὰρ διὰ βραχέων ἐπέστειλα ὑμῖν.
13:22.targetText: And I beg you, brothers, endure the word of the exhortation, for I have also written to you through few words.

groups.note: The actual genitive neuter-plural short/brief adjective βραχέων is substantival in the brief-writing idiom (Thayer1024). English few words names that actual brief written content, not an independently printed λόγοι words noun.

groups.note: The actual perfect passive released participle is predicated of the accusative brother Timotheus as the know-content. English expands that same object/participle content into that ... is released; no independent Greek that conjunction or finite be verb is printed.
